cover.introLabel: Cover: Who is this site for?
cover.introLead: If you have a technology project and need an experienced developer, welcome. I’m Aleksandr Smirnov. I built my first project, an app for recording audio samples, in 2004. In 2006, my hobby became a profession when I joined a well-known software outsourcing company. Since then, I’ve worked in backend, frontend and full-stack development, led teams, and tried vibe coding. Frontend development is my specialty, and I’m always up for trying something new.
cover.skillsLabel: Falling blocks assemble a skills grid: React, TypeScript, Effector, MobX, Webpack, Storybook, Astro JS, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Gemini, DeepSeek, iOS, Android, GitHub, GitLab, Docker, Python
cover.helpLead: I can handle the full development cycle, from writing the specification to delivering a working product. This could be an app, a website, a service, an admin system, AI tool integrations, social media integrations, bots, analytics, A/B testing and much more. I can oversee the work of AI agents and ensure strong security and high performance.
cover.helpFigure: A processor with an array of transistors
cover.startLead: The atlas traces my career back 20 years, starting with what I’m doing today.
cover.startNote: Most of the projects I’ve worked on are covered by NDAs, so I can share only certain details and links.

hobbies.title: What I do away from the screen
hobbies.imageAlt: A paddleboarder on a mountain lake surrounded by pines
paragraphs: I love being outdoors, hiking in the mountains and paddling on rivers and lakes. I have a few paddleboards and boats and have covered dozens of kilometers on them.
In the warmer months, I live in the countryside and go biking and riding my enduro motorcycle.
I’m interested in history. I sometimes read history books, but I mostly listen to lectures. I can listen for hours while exercising or out on a walk.
I’ve spent my life learning and enjoy talking and sharing what I know with people who are curious about a wide range of subjects.

chapterSummaries.2026: AI tools, maintenance for small projects, a media platform for a nonprofit, and a language-learning app. PinNote sends feedback on page elements to an AI coding agent.
chapterSummaries.2023: A strong team, AI-powered trading agents and signals, experiments with trading features, and hackathon-style tournaments.
chapterSummaries.2017: Akma was a trading platform for CFDs, stocks, forex and options. I worked on its core with a frontend team of around 20 developers, using MobX and TypeScript.
chapterSummaries.2015: Fintech and binary options. I built a jQuery MVP in a week, then we grew the team and moved from Backbone to React.
chapterSummaries.2010: Full-stack development on a video upload and playback service, a cloud file service, and a Backbone frontend.
chapterSummaries.2009: A PHP and Microsoft SQL Server CMS and plugins for German government agencies, a WYSIWYG editor, and tools to export Excel and Word documents to HTML.
chapterSummaries.2006: JavaScript and frontend development for T-Mobile, including an accessible, W3C-compliant component library with IE6 support, and a product catalog and CRM built with ExtJS.

01.title: Free time
01.text: When I worked full-time, I had plenty of free time and kept putting things off. Now I’m short on it. The irony is that thanks to AI, writing code by hand takes up at most 15% of my time. The rest goes into defining the problem, designing the architecture, checking the work and seeing it through.

02.title: Media platform
02.text: I’m building a media platform for a nonprofit. It includes a blog, an article catalog, comments, public and restricted content, a headless CMS for authors, an admin system and a CRM.

03.title: Learning languages
03.text: One of my recent projects is a language-learning app with several ways to learn a range of popular languages. It started as a learning aid for my son, and I ended up getting hooked along with relatives and friends.

04.title: PinNote
04.text: I built a local tool for reviewing websites. Leave a comment on any page element and PinNote sends it to an AI coding agent with the element’s DOM context. You can approve the fix in the same panel. I built it after getting tired of constantly switching back to the agent while refining a project.

05.title: Between projects
05.text: I maintain a few small projects that take up little of my time. An update, a check or a fix gives me a welcome change of pace.

01.title: The team
01.text: I was a senior developer on a small, close-knit team. It was the most professional group I’ve worked with.

02.title: iOS, Android and Telegram
02.text: We developed and maintained the app for the web, iOS, Android and Telegram. A configuration file let us enable different features on each platform.

03.title: A bet on AI
03.text: Alongside standard trading tools, we invested in AI. We developed trading agents and signals before they became a trend in the industry.

04.title: Moving at rocket speed
04.text: We got three times as much done as on my previous project. We kept experimenting with features, from professional trading tools to game-like experiences.

05.title: Tournaments
05.text: We held tournaments for users from time to time, usually building them in a hackathon format. We had to move quickly and think creatively. At the same time, AI became an essential tool for coding.

01.title: Trading platform
01.text: Akma was a large trading platform with millions of users. It offered CFDs, stocks, forex and options and served international clients exclusively.

02.title: Team and processes
02.text: I joined as a frontend team lead and senior developer. The frontend team had around 20 developers. I made architecture decisions, hired developers and organized team syncs and offsites. The company held a hackathon every year, and I entered every time. The competition was fierce, and the prizes were worth it.

03.title: Platform core and other teams
03.text: I worked on the Platform team, which owned the project’s core. I also spent time with other teams building the frontend for a crypto wallet and integrating trading charts. We started with Flux and JavaScript and later moved state management to MobX and TypeScript.

01.title: A jQuery MVP
01.text: Interselect was a fintech platform for binary options, a popular product at the time. I joined when the team had about 10 people. I built the first version with jQuery in a week as an MVP to test the idea.

02.title: Backbone → React
02.text: Once the platform turned a profit, we rewrote it with Backbone. The team grew roughly tenfold over a few years. I led four frontend developers and handled architecture, hiring and team meetings. Next came a major migration from Backbone to React.

01.title: On both sides of the API
01.text: I worked as a full-stack developer on several projects, building frontend and backend features and connecting the two.

02.title: Video and cloud storage
02.text: I worked on a video upload and playback service and a cloud file service, building both user interfaces and server-side logic.

03.title: Structuring the frontend
03.text: I introduced Backbone, a new library at the time. The frontend became a standalone application with its own structure.

01.title: On the server side
01.text: I built a CMS and PHP plugins for software used by German government agencies. We stored the data in Microsoft SQL Server.

02.title: Working as a team
02.text: We were a team of six: two backend developers, two frontend developers, a tester and a product manager. I was one of the backend developers.

03.title: Editor and export tools
03.text: I built a WYSIWYG editor from scratch and wrote plugins to export Excel and Word documents to HTML.

01.title: My first JavaScript role
01.text: I worked on a T-Mobile project and was responsible for JavaScript. This was the start of the professional experience covered in this atlas.

02.title: Beyond the code
02.text: I became a team lead in my second year and traveled abroad several times to learn from colleagues and share what we knew.

03.title: Catalog and CRM
03.text: I built a product catalog and CRM using ExtJS.

04.title: Component library
04.text: I created a component library for the T-Mobile online store. It supported browsers going back to IE6 and met all accessibility requirements and W3C validation checks.

01.title: What I’m looking for
01.text: I’m looking for a senior frontend developer role. I take on one-off assignments and small projects, and work with startups. I’m open to part-time or full-time work.
bullets: Flexible hours so I can step away when needed and finish the work later.
